title: education/students
description: One row per enrolled pupil. The pupils. Enrolments, grades and attendance all point back here, and the guardian contact details are what a parent portal would use.

id.description: Surrogate primary key, sequential from 1. Use this for joins rather than the student code.

school_id.description: Which school the pupil attends. Always a school that teaches a stage appropriate to their age.

student_code.description: The pupil's reference at the centre, printed on a student card and used on every internal list.

full_name.description: Spanish name with both surnames, as it appears on the school register.

birth_date.description: Date of birth. Always consistent with the stage the pupil is enrolled in -- a Bachillerato student is 16 to 18, a Primaria pupil 6 to 12.

sex.description: Recorded sex, split close to evenly. Present because official Spanish education statistics are reported broken down by it.

stage.description: Which educational stage the pupil is currently in, derived from their age and consistent with the courses they are enrolled in.

year_level.description: Year within the stage, numbered from 1 and matching the pupil's age within that stage.

guardian_name.description: Parent or guardian, usually sharing one of the pupil's surnames -- which is exactly what Spanish naming produces and what a family-matching feature should be tested against.

guardian_phone.description: Guardian's mobile number in Spanish format. Never empty, because a school cannot enrol a minor without a contact number.

guardian_email.description: Guardian's email on the reserved example.com domain. Empty for about 14% of families, which is the gap any parent-portal rollout runs into.

enrolled_on.description: Date the pupil joined the school, always the start of an academic year.
